The permanent collection of Kunsthaus Wien comprises 412 works as of 31 December 2023, encompassing oil paintings, works on paper, sculpture, photography, and selected decorative art objects. Kunsthaus Wien has maintained an active provenance research programme since 2003, consistent with the Washington Principles on Nazi-Confiscated Art (1998) and the Terezin Declaration (2009), to which the Republic of Austria is a signatory. In 2023, the provenance research team, comprising Dr. Sonja Riegler-Bauer and external researcher Dr. Pavel Schwartz-Horowitz, completed reviews of 23 works with incomplete interwar provenance chains. As a result of this review, two works were identified as having been subject to forced sale or confiscation during the National Socialist period. Following negotiations conducted through the Austrian Commission for Provenance Research (Kommission für Provenienzforschung), an agreement was reached with the legal heirs of Dr. Felix Goldberger-Haas, represented by attorney Mag. Claudia Feldkirchner (Vienna) on behalf of the Goldberger-Haas Family Foundation (registered in Zurich). The two works — KWM-1997-011 and KWM-1997-014, both acquired by the institution at auction in Vienna in 1997 — were formally transferred to the heirs on 12 September 2023. No financial consideration was paid; the transfer was effected as a full restitution. The institution recorded a write-down of €210,000 against the collection valuation for these two works, which had carried a combined insurance value of €210,000 based on the 2020 appraisal. Visitor origin data is collected through voluntary post-visit surveys administered via digital kiosk at the museum exit and through the ticketing system's optional postcode field. In 2023, usable demographic data was collected for 31,840 visitors, representing 33.6% of total attendance. The institution acknowledges that this sample is self-selected and may not be fully representative of the total visitor population; however, it is consistent with the methodology used in previous years and therefore permits year-on-year trend comparison. Of the surveyed visitors, 38.4% were Vienna residents (postcode prefix 1XXX), 14.2% were Austrian residents from outside Vienna, 21.7% were German-speaking visitors from Germany and Switzerland, 11.3% were visitors from other EU member states, and 14.4% were international visitors from outside the EU. The largest non-German-speaking nationality groups were Italian (3.2%), Czech (2.8%), and American (2.1%). First-time visitors accounted for 61.3% of surveyed respondents, while repeat visitors (those who had attended at least once in the previous twelve months) accounted for 38.7%. The age distribution of surveyed visitors showed a concentration in the 35–54 age bracket, which accounted for 41.2% of respondents. Visitors aged 18–34 represented 22.8%, those aged 55–69 represented 24.6%, and those aged 70 and above represented 8.1%. Visitors under 18 are tracked separately through group booking records and accounted for 3.3% of total attendance, primarily through organised school visits. 4.3 Exhibition Attendance Detail

The institution ran two major temporary exhibitions in 2023 in addition to the permanent collection galleries, which remain open throughout the year. The Secession Echoes retrospective, curated by Dr. Sonja Riegler-Bauer with guest co-curator Prof. Anna Dvořáková-Bloch (Charles University Prague), explored the legacy of the Vienna Secession in Central European painting from 1897 to 1938. It ran from 4 March to 21 May 2023 and attracted 28,412 ticketed visitors over its eleven-week run. This was the most attended temporary exhibition in the institution's history, exceeding the previous record of 24,118 visitors set by the 2017 exhibition Klimt und seine Zeitgenossen. A companion catalogue, edited by Dr. Riegler-Bauer, was published by Verlag Anton Schroll & Co. (Vienna) and sold 1,847 copies through the museum shop and online during 2023. The Farbe und Stille exhibition, a dual institutional project co-presented with the Lentos Kunstmuseum Linz and curated by Mag. 5. Exhibition Programme and Curatorial Activity

5.1 Curatorial Philosophy and 2023 Programme Overview

The curatorial direction of Kunsthaus Wien is governed by the five-year Exhibition Strategy 2021–2025, approved by the Board of Trustees in November 2020 (resolution KWM-BOARD- 2020-11-R03). The strategy prioritises three thematic pillars: the recontextualisation of canonical Central European modernism through contemporary scholarly perspectives; the amplification of historically underrepresented voices within the Central European art tradition, with particular emphasis on women artists and artists from successor states of the Austro- Hungarian Empire; and the fostering of cross-institutional dialogue through co-curated and travelling exhibitions with partner institutions. The 2023 programme was the third year of execution under this strategy and demonstrated strong alignment with all three pillars. Secession Echoes addressed the first and third pillars through its scholarly reappraisal of Secessionist influence and its collaboration with the Charles University Prague. Farbe und Stille addressed the second pillar through its focus on women painters active in the postwar Austrian and Czechoslovak art scenes. The permanent collection galleries underwent a partial rehang in July 2023, with twelve works rotated to storage and eight previously stored works brought to display, increasing the proportion of works by women artists in the permanent display from 18.3% to 24.7%. 5.2 Loan Agreements and Inter-Institutional Exchanges

Kunsthaus Wien participated in nine inter-institutional loan arrangements during 2023, comprising six outgoing loans and three incoming loans. Outgoing loans are managed under the institution's standard Loan Agreement template (KWM-LEGAL-LOAN-TMPL-v4, last revised February 2022) and require mandatory approval by the Director General for loans exceeding 60 days in duration or involving works with an individual insurance valuation above €100,000. All six outgoing loans in 2023 fell within delegated approval authority. The three incoming loans are governed by the lending institution's own agreement templates and have been reviewed by the institution's legal counsel, Mag. Gerhard Praxmarer of Praxmarer Rechtsanwälte GmbH (Vienna). The most significant incoming loan is a group of four drawings attributed to Egon Schiele (collection of the Szépművészeti Múzeum Budapest, inventory numbers SZM-GR-1934-0041 through 0044), loaned for the Secession Echoes exhibition under agreement ref. SZM-LOAN-2023-KWM-01, governed by Hungarian law, with insurance coverage provided by the Szépművészeti Múzeum under its own institutional policy with Allianz Hungária. Kunsthaus Wien assumed no insurance liability for these works during transit or display. 5.3 Planned 2024 Programme

The 2024 exhibition calendar has been approved in outline by the Board and comprises two major temporary exhibitions and one medium-scale focus exhibition. The major spring exhibition, provisionally im Wien der Zwischenkriegszeit, is scheduled to open 8 March 2024 and run until 26 May 2024. 9. Strategic Outlook and Risk Register

9.1 Strategic Priorities for 2024–2025

The final two years of the 2021–2025 Strategic Plan will be characterised by consolidation, evaluation, and preparation for the next planning cycle. Three strategic priorities have been identified by the Director General and endorsed by the Board at the December 2023 meeting. First, the institution will pursue a targeted acquisition campaign in the area of postwar Austrian women artists, for which the Acquisitions Committee has pre-approved a ring-fenced budget of €400,000 drawn from the Conservation Reserve Fund pending a formal Board resolution expected in March 2024. Dr. Riegler-Bauer has identified seven priority works across five artists whose estates or existing owners have expressed willingness to negotiate. The most significant target is a large-format triptych by Herta Kronauer-Weiß (1928–2004), currently in a private collection in Graz, which is estimated to be available for purchase at between €150,000 and €220,000. Second, the institution will undertake a full governance review in 2024, the first since 2017, to be conducted by external facilitator Dr. Monika Ehrenfeld-Strasser of Ehrenfeld Consulting (Vienna). The review will examine Board composition, trustee term limits, the delegation of authority matrix, and conflicts of interest policy. The engagement has been budgeted at €28,000 and will conclude with a written report to the Board no later than 30 September 2024. Third, and strategically most significant, the institution will formally launch a capital campaign in 2024 targeting a €2,000,000 increase in the endowment over a five-year horizon. The campaign will be led by a newly appointed Development Director, a role approved by the Board in October 2023 and currently in the final stages of recruitment. The shortlisted candidates are Mag. Florian Weidinger-Holub (currently Head of Development at the Vienna Philharmonic Foundation) and Dr. Brigitte Samuels-Baumann (currently Director of Philanthropy at the Kunsthistorisches Museum).

Kunsthaus Wien has maintained an active provenance research programme since 2003, consistent with the Washington Principles on Nazi-Confiscated Art (1998) and the Terezin Declaration (2009), to which the Republic of Austria is a signatory. In 2023, the provenance research team, comprising Dr. Sonja Riegler-Bauer and external researcher Dr. Pavel Schwartz-Horowitz, completed reviews of 23 works with incomplete interwar provenance chains. As a result of this review, two works were identified as having been subject to forced sale or confiscation during the National Socialist period. Following negotiations conducted through the Austrian Commission for Provenance Research (Kommission für Provenienzforschung), an agreement was reached with the legal heirs of Dr. Felix Goldberger-Haas, represented by attorney Mag. Claudia Feldkirchner (Vienna) on behalf of the Goldberger-Haas Family Foundation (registered in Zurich). The two works — KWM-1997-011 and KWM-1997-014, both acquired by the institution at auction in Vienna in 1997 — were formally transferred to the heirs on 12 September 2023. 5. Exhibition Programme and Curatorial Activity

5.1 Curatorial Philosophy and 2023 Programme Overview

The curatorial direction of Kunsthaus Wien is governed by the five-year Exhibition Strategy 2021–2025, approved by the Board of Trustees in November 2020 (resolution KWM-BOARD- 2020-11-R03). The strategy prioritises three thematic pillars: the recontextualisation of canonical Central European modernism through contemporary scholarly perspectives; the amplification of historically underrepresented voices within the Central European art tradition, with particular emphasis on women artists and artists from successor states of the Austro- Hungarian Empire; and the fostering of cross-institutional dialogue through co-curated and travelling exhibitions with partner institutions. The 2023 programme was the third year of execution under this strategy and demonstrated strong alignment with all three pillars. Secession Echoes addressed the first and third pillars through its scholarly reappraisal of Secessionist influence and its collaboration with the Charles University Prague. Farbe und Stille addressed the second pillar through its focus on women painters active in the postwar Austrian and Czechoslovak art scenes. The permanent collection galleries underwent a partial rehang in July 2023, with twelve works rotated to storage and eight previously stored works brought to display, increasing the proportion of works by women artists in the permanent display from 18.3% to 24.7%. 5.2 Loan Agreements and Inter-Institutional Exchanges

A note of caution is warranted regarding the interpretation of visitor statistics presented in Section 4. The total figure of 94,620 visitors represents gross recorded admissions and should not be used without adjustment for certain operational factors. Specifically, holders of the annual Kunsthaus Pass (of whom there were 1,847 active passholders as of 31 December 2023) are recorded as individual admissions on each visit, meaning frequent visitors may be counted multiple times within the annual total. Internal modelling by Mag. Zehetgruber's team suggests that adjusting for estimated repeat pass-holder visits would reduce the effective unique visitor count to approximately 81,200–83,400, though this estimate carries significant uncertainty. 9.1 Strategic Priorities for 2024–2025

The final two years of the 2021–2025 Strategic Plan will be characterised by consolidation, evaluation, and preparation for the next planning cycle. Three strategic priorities have been identified by the Director General and endorsed by the Board at the December 2023 meeting. 5. Exhibition Programme and Curatorial Activity

5.1 Curatorial Philosophy and 2023 Programme Overview

The curatorial direction of Kunsthaus Wien is governed by the five-year Exhibition Strategy 2021–2025, approved by the Board of Trustees in November 2020 (resolution KWM-BOARD- 2020-11-R03). The strategy prioritises three thematic pillars: the recontextualisation of canonical Central European modernism through contemporary scholarly perspectives; the amplification of historically underrepresented voices within the Central European art tradition, with particular emphasis on women artists and artists from successor states of the Austro- Hungarian Empire; and the fostering of cross-institutional dialogue through co-curated and travelling exhibitions with partner institutions. The 2023 programme was the third year of execution under this strategy and demonstrated strong alignment with all three pillars. Secession Echoes addressed the first and third pillars through its scholarly reappraisal of Secessionist influence and its collaboration with the Charles University Prague. Farbe und Stille addressed the second pillar through its focus on women painters active in the postwar Austrian and Czechoslovak art scenes. The permanent collection galleries underwent a partial rehang in July 2023, with twelve works rotated to storage and eight previously stored works brought to display, increasing the proportion of works by women artists in the permanent display from 18.3% to 24.7%. 5.2 Loan Agreements and Inter-Institutional Exchanges

Kunsthaus Wien participated in nine inter-institutional loan arrangements during 2023, comprising six outgoing loans and three incoming loans. 9. Strategic Outlook and Risk Register

9.1 Strategic Priorities for 2024–2025

The final two years of the 2021–2025 Strategic Plan will be characterised by consolidation, evaluation, and preparation for the next planning cycle. Three strategic priorities have been identified by the Director General and endorsed by the Board at the December 2023 meeting. First, the institution will pursue a targeted acquisition campaign in the area of postwar Austrian women artists, for which the Acquisitions Committee has pre-approved a ring-fenced budget of €400,000 drawn from the Conservation Reserve Fund pending a formal Board resolution expected in March 2024. Dr. Riegler-Bauer has identified seven priority works across five artists whose estates or existing owners have expressed willingness to negotiate. The most significant target is a large-format triptych by Herta Kronauer-Weiß (1928–2004), currently in a private collection in Graz, which is estimated to be available for purchase at between €150,000 and €220,000. Second, the institution will undertake a full governance review in 2024, the first since 2017, to be conducted by external facilitator Dr. Monika Ehrenfeld-Strasser of Ehrenfeld Consulting (Vienna). The review will examine Board composition, trustee term limits, the delegation of authority matrix, and conflicts of interest policy. The engagement has been budgeted at €28,000 and will conclude with a written report to the Board no later than 30 September 2024. Third, and strategically most significant, the institution will formally launch a capital campaign in 2024 targeting a €2,000,000 increase in the endowment over a five-year horizon. The campaign will be led by a newly appointed Development Director, a role approved by the Board in October 2023 and currently in the final stages of recruitment. The shortlisted candidates are Mag. Florian Weidinger-Holub (currently Head of Development at the Vienna Philharmonic Foundation) and Dr. Brigitte Samuels-Baumann (currently Director of Philanthropy at the Kunsthistorisches Museum).

1. Director General's Foreword

The year 2023 marked a period of remarkable transformation and consolidation for Kunsthaus Wien. Under the continued stewardship of the Board of Trustees and with the tireless dedication of our 87 permanent staff members and 34 part-time associates, we achieved a record-breaking institutional performance that exceeded nearly every measurable target set in our 2021–2025 Strategic Plan. Our Director General, Dr. Maximilian Oberhuber-Steiner, assumed the post in January 2022 following the retirement of his predecessor, Dr. Eleonore Vásárhelyi, and has since led the institution through two major exhibition cycles, one significant acquisition campaign, and a complete overhaul of our digital infrastructure. This report covers the full fiscal year from 1 January to 31 December 2023 and represents the most comprehensive institutional self- assessment Kunsthaus Wien has produced in its thirty-one-year history. Among the highlights of 2023, we note the successful conclusion of the Secession Echoes retrospective in the spring, which attracted 28,412 visitors over its eleven-week run and became the most attended temporary exhibition in our institutional history. The autumn season brought the equally celebrated dual exhibition Farbe und Stille, co-organised with the Lentos Kunstmuseum Linz, which drew 19,847 visitors between September and November. Total annual footfall reached 94,620 visitors, surpassing the previous record of 88,340 set in 2019. From a financial perspective, the institution closed the year with total operating revenue of €6,284,500, against total expenditure of €5,917,340, yielding a modest but strategically meaningful surplus of €367,160. This surplus has been allocated in full to the Conservation Reserve Fund, consistent with the Board resolution of March 2023. The institution received public funding from the City of Vienna's Kulturabteilung (MA 7) in the amount of €2,100,000 and from the Austrian Federal Chancellery's Kunstsektion in the amount of €850,000, totalling €2,950,000 in public subsidy, which represented 46.9% of total operating revenue. We enter 2024 with cautious optimism. The global art market has shown signs of softening following exceptional growth in 2021 and 2022, and donor appetite for large-scale capital gifts has become more selective. Nevertheless, Kunsthaus Wien is well-positioned: our endowment stands at €4,750,000, our collection is insured at replacement value for €38,200,000, and our institutional partnerships span fourteen countries across Europe and the Americas. This document is intended solely for internal governance purposes and the use of the Board of Trustees, senior management, and approved statutory auditors.

3. Permanent Collection Report

3.1 Collection Overview

The permanent collection of Kunsthaus Wien comprises 412 works as of 31 December 2023, encompassing oil paintings, works on paper, sculpture, photography, and selected decorative art objects. The collection spans the period from approximately 1875 to 1979, with the highest density of holdings concentrated in the Viennese Secession and its immediate aftermath (1897–1930), the interwar Neue Sachlichkeit movement as it manifested in Central Europe, and the postwar Austrian avant-garde of the 1950s and 1960s. During 2023, the collection grew by seven works through purchase and one work through donation, while two works were deaccessioned following a provenance review and restitution agreement concluded with the estate of Dr. Felix Goldberger-Haas, as detailed in Section 3.4 of this report. The net collection stood at 412 works at year-end, compared to 406 works at the close of 2022. The collection is currently valued for insurance purposes at €38,200,000, based on an independent appraisal conducted by Rathmore & Schreiber Kunstgutachter GmbH (Vienna/Zurich) in September 2023. This represents a 6.1% increase over the previous insurance valuation of €35,990,000 established in 2020. Individual work valuations are maintained in the internal Collection Management System (CMS) under restricted access and are not disclosed in this institutional document. The five most valuable individual works in the collection, based on current insurance valuation, are not identified by name in this report in accordance with security protocol MDU-SEC-2019- 03 approved by the Board. 3. Permanent Collection Report

3.1 Collection Overview

The permanent collection of Kunsthaus Wien comprises 412 works as of 31 December 2023, encompassing oil paintings, works on paper, sculpture, photography, and selected decorative art objects. The collection spans the period from approximately 1875 to 1979, with the highest density of holdings concentrated in the Viennese Secession and its immediate aftermath (1897–1930), the interwar Neue Sachlichkeit movement as it manifested in Central Europe, and the postwar Austrian avant-garde of the 1950s and 1960s. During 2023, the collection grew by seven works through purchase and one work through donation, while two works were deaccessioned following a provenance review and restitution agreement concluded with the estate of Dr. Felix Goldberger-Haas, as detailed in Section 3.4 of this report. The net collection stood at 412 works at year-end, compared to 406 works at the close of 2022. The collection is currently valued for insurance purposes at €38,200,000, based on an independent appraisal conducted by Rathmore & Schreiber Kunstgutachter GmbH (Vienna/Zurich) in September 2023. Kunsthaus Wien has maintained an active provenance research programme since 2003, consistent with the Washington Principles on Nazi-Confiscated Art (1998) and the Terezin Declaration (2009), to which the Republic of Austria is a signatory. In 2023, the provenance research team, comprising Dr. Sonja Riegler-Bauer and external researcher Dr. Pavel Schwartz-Horowitz, completed reviews of 23 works with incomplete interwar provenance chains. The two works — KWM-1997-011 and KWM-1997-014, both acquired by the institution at auction in Vienna in 1997 — were formally transferred to the heirs on 12 September 2023. No financial consideration was paid; the transfer was effected as a full restitution. The institution recorded a write-down of €210,000 against the collection valuation for these two works, which had carried a combined insurance value of €210,000 based on the 2020 appraisal. 5. Exhibition Programme and Curatorial Activity

5.1 Curatorial Philosophy and 2023 Programme Overview

The curatorial direction of Kunsthaus Wien is governed by the five-year Exhibition Strategy 2021–2025, approved by the Board of Trustees in November 2020 (resolution KWM-BOARD- 2020-11-R03). The strategy prioritises three thematic pillars: the recontextualisation of canonical Central European modernism through contemporary scholarly perspectives; the amplification of historically underrepresented voices within the Central European art tradition, with particular emphasis on women artists and artists from successor states of the Austro- Hungarian Empire; and the fostering of cross-institutional dialogue through co-curated and travelling exhibitions with partner institutions. The 2023 programme was the third year of execution under this strategy and demonstrated strong alignment with all three pillars. Secession Echoes addressed the first and third pillars through its scholarly reappraisal of Secessionist influence and its collaboration with the Charles University Prague. Farbe und Stille addressed the second pillar through its focus on women painters active in the postwar Austrian and Czechoslovak art scenes. The permanent collection galleries underwent a partial rehang in July 2023, with twelve works rotated to storage and eight previously stored works brought to display, increasing the proportion of works by women artists in the permanent display from 18.3% to 24.7%. 5.2 Loan Agreements and Inter-Institutional Exchanges

9. Strategic Outlook and Risk Register

9.1 Strategic Priorities for 2024–2025

The final two years of the 2021–2025 Strategic Plan will be characterised by consolidation, evaluation, and preparation for the next planning cycle. Three strategic priorities have been identified by the Director General and endorsed by the Board at the December 2023 meeting. First, the institution will pursue a targeted acquisition campaign in the area of postwar Austrian women artists, for which the Acquisitions Committee has pre-approved a ring-fenced budget of €400,000 drawn from the Conservation Reserve Fund pending a formal Board resolution expected in March 2024. Dr. Riegler-Bauer has identified seven priority works across five artists whose estates or existing owners have expressed willingness to negotiate. The most significant target is a large-format triptych by Herta Kronauer-Weiß (1928–2004), currently in a private collection in Graz, which is estimated to be available for purchase at between €150,000 and €220,000. Second, the institution will undertake a full governance review in 2024, the first since 2017, to be conducted by external facilitator Dr. Monika Ehrenfeld-Strasser of Ehrenfeld Consulting (Vienna). The review will examine Board composition, trustee term limits, the delegation of authority matrix, and conflicts of interest policy. The engagement has been budgeted at €28,000 and will conclude with a written report to the Board no later than 30 September 2024. Third, and strategically most significant, the institution will formally launch a capital campaign in 2024 targeting a €2,000,000 increase in the endowment over a five-year horizon. 3. Permanent Collection Report

3.1 Collection Overview

The permanent collection of Kunsthaus Wien comprises 412 works as of 31 December 2023, encompassing oil paintings, works on paper, sculpture, photography, and selected decorative art objects. The collection spans the period from approximately 1875 to 1979, with the highest density of holdings concentrated in the Viennese Secession and its immediate aftermath (1897–1930), the interwar Neue Sachlichkeit movement as it manifested in Central Europe, and the postwar Austrian avant-garde of the 1950s and 1960s. During 2023, the collection grew by seven works through purchase and one work through donation, while two works were deaccessioned following a provenance review and restitution agreement concluded with the estate of Dr. Felix Goldberger-Haas, as detailed in Section 3.4 of this report. The net collection stood at 412 works at year-end, compared to 406 works at the close of 2022. The collection is currently valued for insurance purposes at €38,200,000, based on an independent appraisal conducted by Rathmore & Schreiber Kunstgutachter GmbH (Vienna/Zurich) in September 2023. This represents a 6.1% increase over the previous insurance valuation of €35,990,000 established in 2020. Individual work valuations are maintained in the internal Collection Management System (CMS) under restricted access and are not disclosed in this institutional document. The five most valuable individual works in the collection, based on current insurance valuation, are not identified by name in this report in accordance with security protocol MDU-SEC-2019- 03 approved by the Board. However, it is noted for governance purposes that the single most valuable work in the collection carries an individual insurance valuation of €4,200,000 and belongs to the early Viennese Expressionist period. 3.2 Acquisitions in 2023

The Acquisitions Committee, chaired by Trustee Mag. 5.1 Curatorial Philosophy and 2023 Programme Overview

The curatorial direction of Kunsthaus Wien is governed by the five-year Exhibition Strategy 2021–2025, approved by the Board of Trustees in November 2020 (resolution KWM-BOARD- 2020-11-R03). The strategy prioritises three thematic pillars: the recontextualisation of canonical Central European modernism through contemporary scholarly perspectives; the amplification of historically underrepresented voices within the Central European art tradition, with particular emphasis on women artists and artists from successor states of the Austro- Hungarian Empire; and the fostering of cross-institutional dialogue through co-curated and travelling exhibitions with partner institutions. The 2023 programme was the third year of execution under this strategy and demonstrated strong alignment with all three pillars. Secession Echoes addressed the first and third pillars through its scholarly reappraisal of Secessionist influence and its collaboration with the Charles University Prague. Farbe und Stille addressed the second pillar through its focus on women painters active in the postwar Austrian and Czechoslovak art scenes. 9.1 Strategic Priorities for 2024–2025

The final two years of the 2021–2025 Strategic Plan will be characterised by consolidation, evaluation, and preparation for the next planning cycle. Three strategic priorities have been identified by the Director General and endorsed by the Board at the December 2023 meeting. First, the institution will pursue a targeted acquisition campaign in the area of postwar Austrian women artists, for which the Acquisitions Committee has pre-approved a ring-fenced budget of €400,000 drawn from the Conservation Reserve Fund pending a formal Board resolution expected in March 2024. Dr. Riegler-Bauer has identified seven priority works across five artists whose estates or existing owners have expressed willingness to negotiate. The most significant target is a large-format triptych by Herta Kronauer-Weiß (1928–2004), currently in a private collection in Graz, which is estimated to be available for purchase at between €150,000 and €220,000. Third, and strategically most significant, the institution will formally launch a capital campaign in 2024 targeting a €2,000,000 increase in the endowment over a five-year horizon. 1. Director General's Foreword

The year 2023 marked a period of remarkable transformation and consolidation for Kunsthaus Wien. Our Director General, Dr. Maximilian Oberhuber-Steiner, assumed the post in January 2022 following the retirement of his predecessor, Dr. Eleonore Vásárhelyi, and has since led the institution through two major exhibition cycles, one significant acquisition campaign, and a complete overhaul of our digital infrastructure. 9.3 Note on Visitor Data Interpretation

A note of caution is warranted regarding the interpretation of visitor statistics presented in Section 4. The total figure of 94,620 visitors represents gross recorded admissions and should not be used without adjustment for certain operational factors. Specifically, holders of the annual Kunsthaus Pass (of whom there were 1,847 active passholders as of 31 December 2023) are recorded as individual admissions on each visit, meaning frequent visitors may be counted multiple times within the annual total. Internal modelling by Mag. Zehetgruber's team suggests that adjusting for estimated repeat pass-holder visits would reduce the effective unique visitor count to approximately 81,200–83,400, though this estimate carries significant uncertainty. Furthermore, school groups are recorded at the point of guided tour commencement, not at point of ticket sale. In instances where a school group visits both the temporary and permanent exhibition spaces within a single visit, the group is counted once, not twice. This practice differs from the methodology used by some peer institutions, which count exhibition-level visits rather than person-level visits. Readers comparing KWM statistics to those of peer institutions should be aware of this methodological difference. 9.4 Correction to 2022 Annual Report

9. Strategic Outlook and Risk Register

9.1 Strategic Priorities for 2024–2025

The final two years of the 2021–2025 Strategic Plan will be characterised by consolidation, evaluation, and preparation for the next planning cycle. Three strategic priorities have been identified by the Director General and endorsed by the Board at the December 2023 meeting. First, the institution will pursue a targeted acquisition campaign in the area of postwar Austrian women artists, for which the Acquisitions Committee has pre-approved a ring-fenced budget of €400,000 drawn from the Conservation Reserve Fund pending a formal Board resolution expected in March 2024. Dr. Riegler-Bauer has identified seven priority works across five artists whose estates or existing owners have expressed willingness to negotiate. The most significant target is a large-format triptych by Herta Kronauer-Weiß (1928–2004), currently in a private collection in Graz, which is estimated to be available for purchase at between €150,000 and €220,000. Second, the institution will undertake a full governance review in 2024, the first since 2017, to be conducted by external facilitator Dr. Monika Ehrenfeld-Strasser of Ehrenfeld Consulting (Vienna). The review will examine Board composition, trustee term limits, the delegation of authority matrix, and conflicts of interest policy. The engagement has been budgeted at €28,000 and will conclude with a written report to the Board no later than 30 September 2024. Third, and strategically most significant, the institution will formally launch a capital campaign in 2024 targeting a €2,000,000 increase in the endowment over a five-year horizon. The campaign will be led by a newly appointed Development Director, a role approved by the Board in October 2023 and currently in the final stages of recruitment. The shortlisted candidates are Mag. Florian Weidinger-Holub (currently Head of Development at the Vienna Philharmonic Foundation) and Dr. Brigitte Samuels-Baumann (currently Director of Philanthropy at the Kunsthistorisches Museum).

3. Permanent Collection Report

3.1 Collection Overview

The permanent collection of Kunsthaus Wien comprises 412 works as of 31 December 2023, encompassing oil paintings, works on paper, sculpture, photography, and selected decorative art objects. The collection spans the period from approximately 1875 to 1979, with the highest density of holdings concentrated in the Viennese Secession and its immediate aftermath (1897–1930), the interwar Neue Sachlichkeit movement as it manifested in Central Europe, and the postwar Austrian avant-garde of the 1950s and 1960s. During 2023, the collection grew by seven works through purchase and one work through donation, while two works were deaccessioned following a provenance review and restitution agreement concluded with the estate of Dr. Felix Goldberger-Haas, as detailed in Section 3.4 of this report. The net collection stood at 412 works at year-end, compared to 406 works at the close of 2022. The collection is currently valued for insurance purposes at €38,200,000, based on an independent appraisal conducted by Rathmore & Schreiber Kunstgutachter GmbH (Vienna/Zurich) in September 2023. This represents a 6.1% increase over the previous insurance valuation of €35,990,000 established in 2020. Individual work valuations are maintained in the internal Collection Management System (CMS) under restricted access and are not disclosed in this institutional document. The five most valuable individual works in the collection, based on current insurance valuation, are not identified by name in this report in accordance with security protocol MDU-SEC-2019- 03 approved by the Board. 9. Strategic Outlook and Risk Register

9.1 Strategic Priorities for 2024–2025

The final two years of the 2021–2025 Strategic Plan will be characterised by consolidation, evaluation, and preparation for the next planning cycle. Three strategic priorities have been identified by the Director General and endorsed by the Board at the December 2023 meeting. First, the institution will pursue a targeted acquisition campaign in the area of postwar Austrian women artists, for which the Acquisitions Committee has pre-approved a ring-fenced budget of €400,000 drawn from the Conservation Reserve Fund pending a formal Board resolution expected in March 2024. Dr. Riegler-Bauer has identified seven priority works across five artists whose estates or existing owners have expressed willingness to negotiate. The most significant target is a large-format triptych by Herta Kronauer-Weiß (1928–2004), currently in a private collection in Graz, which is estimated to be available for purchase at between €150,000 and €220,000. Second, the institution will undertake a full governance review in 2024, the first since 2017, to be conducted by external facilitator Dr. Monika Ehrenfeld-Strasser of Ehrenfeld Consulting (Vienna). The review will examine Board composition, trustee term limits, the delegation of authority matrix, and conflicts of interest policy. The engagement has been budgeted at €28,000 and will conclude with a written report to the Board no later than 30 September 2024. Third, and strategically most significant, the institution will formally launch a capital campaign in 2024 targeting a €2,000,000 increase in the endowment over a five-year horizon. The campaign will be led by a newly appointed Development Director, a role approved by the Board in October 2023 and currently in the final stages of recruitment. The shortlisted candidates are Mag. Visitor origin data is collected through voluntary post-visit surveys administered via digital kiosk at the museum exit and through the ticketing system's optional postcode field. In 2023, usable demographic data was collected for 31,840 visitors, representing 33.6% of total attendance. The institution acknowledges that this sample is self-selected and may not be fully representative of the total visitor population; however, it is consistent with the methodology used in previous years and therefore permits year-on-year trend comparison. Of the surveyed visitors, 38.4% were Vienna residents (postcode prefix 1XXX), 14.2% were Austrian residents from outside Vienna, 21.7% were German-speaking visitors from Germany and Switzerland, 11.3% were visitors from other EU member states, and 14.4% were international visitors from outside the EU. The largest non-German-speaking nationality groups were Italian (3.2%), Czech (2.8%), and American (2.1%). First-time visitors accounted for 61.3% of surveyed respondents, while repeat visitors (those who had attended at least once in the previous twelve months) accounted for 38.7%. The age distribution of surveyed visitors showed a concentration in the 35–54 age bracket, which accounted for 41.2% of respondents. Visitors aged 18–34 represented 22.8%, those aged 55–69 represented 24.6%, and those aged 70 and above represented 8.1%. Visitors under 18 are tracked separately through group booking records and accounted for 3.3% of total attendance, primarily through organised school visits. 4.3 Exhibition Attendance Detail

The institution ran two major temporary exhibitions in 2023 in addition to the permanent collection galleries, which remain open throughout the year. The Secession Echoes retrospective, curated by Dr. Sonja Riegler-Bauer with guest co-curator Prof. Anna Dvořáková-Bloch (Charles University Prague), explored the legacy of the Vienna Secession in Central European painting from 1897 to 1938. It ran from 4 March to 21 May 2023 and attracted 28,412 ticketed visitors over its eleven-week run. This was the most attended temporary exhibition in the institution's history, exceeding the previous record of 24,118 visitors set by the 2017 exhibition Klimt und seine Zeitgenossen. A companion catalogue, edited by Dr. Riegler-Bauer, was published by Verlag Anton Schroll & Co. (Vienna) and sold 1,847 copies through the museum shop and online during 2023. 5. Exhibition Programme and Curatorial Activity

5.1 Curatorial Philosophy and 2023 Programme Overview

The curatorial direction of Kunsthaus Wien is governed by the five-year Exhibition Strategy 2021–2025, approved by the Board of Trustees in November 2020 (resolution KWM-BOARD- 2020-11-R03). The strategy prioritises three thematic pillars: the recontextualisation of canonical Central European modernism through contemporary scholarly perspectives; the amplification of historically underrepresented voices within the Central European art tradition, with particular emphasis on women artists and artists from successor states of the Austro- Hungarian Empire; and the fostering of cross-institutional dialogue through co-curated and travelling exhibitions with partner institutions. The 2023 programme was the third year of execution under this strategy and demonstrated strong alignment with all three pillars. Secession Echoes addressed the first and third pillars through its scholarly reappraisal of Secessionist influence and its collaboration with the Charles University Prague. Farbe und Stille addressed the second pillar through its focus on women painters active in the postwar Austrian and Czechoslovak art scenes. The permanent collection galleries underwent a partial rehang in July 2023, with twelve works rotated to storage and eight previously stored works brought to display, increasing the proportion of works by women artists in the permanent display from 18.3% to 24.7%. 5.2 Loan Agreements and Inter-Institutional Exchanges

Kunsthaus Wien participated in nine inter-institutional loan arrangements during 2023, comprising six outgoing loans and three incoming loans. Outgoing loans are managed under the institution's standard Loan Agreement template (KWM-LEGAL-LOAN-TMPL-v4, last revised February 2022) and require mandatory approval by the Director General for loans exceeding 60 days in duration or involving works with an individual insurance valuation above €100,000. All six outgoing loans in 2023 fell within delegated approval authority. The largest non-German-speaking nationality groups were Italian (3.2%), Czech (2.8%), and American (2.1%). First-time visitors accounted for 61.3% of surveyed respondents, while repeat visitors (those who had attended at least once in the previous twelve months) accounted for 38.7%. 5. Exhibition Programme and Curatorial Activity

5.1 Curatorial Philosophy and 2023 Programme Overview

The curatorial direction of Kunsthaus Wien is governed by the five-year Exhibition Strategy 2021–2025, approved by the Board of Trustees in November 2020 (resolution KWM-BOARD- 2020-11-R03). The strategy prioritises three thematic pillars: the recontextualisation of canonical Central European modernism through contemporary scholarly perspectives; the amplification of historically underrepresented voices within the Central European art tradition, with particular emphasis on women artists and artists from successor states of the Austro- Hungarian Empire; and the fostering of cross-institutional dialogue through co-curated and travelling exhibitions with partner institutions. The 2023 programme was the third year of execution under this strategy and demonstrated strong alignment with all three pillars. Secession Echoes addressed the first and third pillars through its scholarly reappraisal of Secessionist influence and its collaboration with the Charles University Prague. Farbe und Stille addressed the second pillar through its focus on women painters active in the postwar Austrian and Czechoslovak art scenes. The permanent collection galleries underwent a partial rehang in July 2023, with twelve works rotated to storage and eight previously stored works brought to display, increasing the proportion of works by women artists in the permanent display from 18.3% to 24.7%. 5.2 Loan Agreements and Inter-Institutional Exchanges

Kunsthaus Wien participated in nine inter-institutional loan arrangements during 2023, comprising six outgoing loans and three incoming loans. Outgoing loans are managed under the institution's standard Loan Agreement template (KWM-LEGAL-LOAN-TMPL-v4, last revised February 2022) and require mandatory approval by the Director General for loans exceeding 60 days in duration or involving works with an individual insurance valuation above €100,000. All six outgoing loans in 2023 fell within delegated approval authority.
